description: Approach-channel geometry of the catalytic serine in PLAP, human TNAP and E. coli AP
code:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, json
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plap=np.load("out/plap_dimer.npy"); tn=np.load("out/tnap_dimer.npy"); ec=np.load("out/ecoli_dimer.npy")
# catalytic Ser OG for each
def getOG(path_kind):
    pass
three2one={'SER':'S'}
def ser_og_pdb(f,resi):
    for l in open(f):
        if l.startswith("ATOM  ") and l[21]=="A" and l[12:16].strip()=="OG" and int(l[22:26])==resi:
            return np.array([float(l[30:38]),float(l[38:46]),float(l[46:54])])
og_p=ser_og_pdb("out/1EW2.pdb",92); og_e=ser_og_pdb("out/1ALK.pdb",102)
cif=open("out/7YIW.cif").read().split("\n")
i=[k for k,l in enumerate(cif) if l.startswith("_atom_site.")]; hdr=[cif[k].strip() for k in i]; cols={h:n for n,h in enumerate(hdr)}
rec=[p for p in (l.split() for l in cif[i[-1]+1:]) if len(p)==len(hdr)]
def C(p,n): return p[cols["_atom_site."+n]]
og_t=np.array([[float(C(p,"Cartn_x")),float(C(p,"Cartn_y")),float(C(p,"Cartn_z"))] for p in rec
    if C(p,"auth_asym_id")=="A" and C(p,"label_atom_id")=="OG" and int(C(p,"auth_seq_id"))==110][0])

rng=np.random.default_rng(1); V=rng.normal(size=(4000,3)); V/=np.linalg.norm(V,axis=1)[:,None]
rs=np.arange(4.0,20.01,0.5)
def prof(atoms,ctr):
    sub=atoms[np.linalg.norm(atoms-ctr,axis=1)<40]; kd=cKDTree(sub)
    pts=(ctr[None,None,:]+V[:,None,:]*rs[None,:,None]).reshape(-1,3)
    d,_=kd.query(pts,k=1); return d.reshape(len(V),len(rs))
P={"PLAP (1EW2)":prof(plap,og_p),"human TNAP (7YIW)":prof(tn,og_t),"E. coli AP (1ALK)":prof(ec,og_e)}
rows=[]
for nm,d in P.items():
    clear=d.min(1)
    rows.append(dict(enzyme=nm,
        widest_channel_A=round(float(clear.max()),2),
        frac_dirs_clearance_gt3A=round(float((clear>3.0).mean()),3),
        frac_dirs_clearance_gt4A=round(float((clear>4.0).mean()),3),
        frac_dirs_clearance_gt5A=round(float((clear>5.0).mean()),3)))
R=pd.DataFrame(rows); R.to_csv("out/active_site_accessibility.csv",index=False)
print("Rays cast from the catalytic Ser OG, 4000 directions, sampled 4-20 A.")
print("'clearance' = min distance to any protein atom along a ray; >3 A means a small molecule can pass,")
print(">5 A means a bulky group (e.g. a phosphoresidue on a folded protein) could approach.")
print(R.to_string(index=False))

fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.4))
ax=axes[0]
for nm,d in P.items():
    ax.plot(rs, np.percentile(d,99,axis=0), lw=2, label=nm+" (99th pct)")
    ax.plot(rs, d.mean(0), lw=1, ls="--", alpha=.7, color=ax.lines[-1].get_color(), label=nm+" (mean)")
ax.set_xlabel("distance from catalytic Ser OG (Å)"); ax.set_ylabel("clearance to nearest protein atom (Å)")
ax.set_title("Approach channel to the catalytic serine"); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=.3)
ax=axes[1]
for nm,d in P.items():
    ax.hist(d.min(1),bins=np.arange(0,6,0.15),histtype="step",lw=2,label=nm,density=True)
ax.set_xlabel("tightest clearance along a ray (Å)"); ax.set_ylabel("density of directions")
ax.set_title("Distribution of approach-channel widths"); ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=.3)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
